_about: Recorded Kokoro af_heart speech (24 kHz, speed 1.0): 'duration' is the length of each line's synthesized clip in seconds, as voice script lays it out. Text and timings only, no audio. Recorded 2026-10-09 on Linux with `showtime voice script`'s own synthesis (tts.synthesize), to check script.estimate_fit against real timings.

lines.text: Every morning, a quiet machine on your desk decides how your day will go, and almost nobody notices it.
Most video tools ask you to upload your footage, pay a monthly fee, and wait in a queue while someone else's computer does the work.
Showtime flips that around. Your agent writes the scenes, and your own laptop renders every frame, with no accounts, no keys and no uploads.
Narration comes from a local voice, so the words, the timing and the captions all stay on your machine.
Music, sound effects and loudness are mixed to the standard that phones and streaming platforms expect, without a single manual slider.
In one afternoon a small team turned a changelog into a sixty second launch film, and nobody opened an editor.
That is the whole idea: tell your agent what you want to show, and let your machine put on the show.
